reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality emerges from the distinction between formal and dimensional means-end-capacities. Formal capacity (g) reflects abstract reasoning power independent of physical instantiation, whereas dimensional capacity (s) reflects embodied skill within a given perceptual-motor domain. These operate in complementary spaces: g governs logical inference paths, while s determines feasibility of execution. The composite capacity C = g ⊕ s captures holistic cognition. Failure occurs when attempting to equate g across differing s domains (e.g., comparing parrot vs. elephant), due to non-overlapping discriminanda-manipulanda structures. This leads to a breakdown in measurement coherence. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian model misalignment when prior beliefs about g are applied across incompatible s contexts. In GSE, it causes policy collapse during state transitions where s changes abruptly without corresponding g adjustment. The dual structure implies that true comparative intelligence requires controlled dimensional alignment—a principle that underpins both cognitive modeling and adaptive control theory.
